main_text.p: finistro, atque infelici eventu? Dictavit hoc seculum antiquum in Nonio Asprenate, qui coram Cæsare Augusto Trojam ludens, crure ex equi lapsu est debilitatus. Testimonio insuper est, ut ad recentiores veniam, infelix Francisci Borbonii Anchiani casus, qui miserabili in ludo, luxatâ cervice, confractoque cerebro sternitur. Nec Thuan. libr.3. Histor. Tom.1.oblivioni traditum Henrici ejus nominis secundi fatum, in publicâ celebritate, cum Montgomerio Comite concurrentis. Confractis enim utrinque hastis, ex trunci ictu, qui forte per apertam cassidem in oculum penetraverat, secundariâ percussione vulnus accepit, quo intra undecimum diem confectus, naturæ cessit. Idem quod accidit in Germaniâ fortissimo Principi Friderico Thuringiæ Landgravio. Cum enim ille voluptatis & honoris gratiâ

page.notes: The left-margin note "Thuan. libr.3. Hiftor. Tom.1." is transcribed as "Thuan. libr.3. Histor. Tom.1." with long s read as s. A black dot stands in the text after "Henrici" and before "ejus" and is not transcribed as a reference mark, since no matching mark appears in the note. The running head is letter-spaced in print as "P. V O E T". The last word of the page is continued on the next page, with the catchword "co-" printed at the lower right.
